catalog_quote: c) La tonologie est du type normal (comparativement au Proto-Bantu). On rencontre néamoins quelques mots avec une tonalité contraire à celle à laquelle on s'attendrait en lingɔmbɛ ou en lomɔ́ngo : mbúlá, pluie, mai, eau; bibende, fers... Mais comme la tonologie de certains parlers de la Ngiri présente des spécifités qui dépendent généralement de la structure syntaxique, peut-être faudra-t-il ici attendre une étude plus approfondie qui devra être appuyée par le recours au magnétophone. ... II. Substantifs. Les préfixes sont généralement bas.
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress
sweep_summary: Loi-Likila (balo1261) is not in the catalog. Both stress-titled bibliography items (Halle & Kenstowicz 1991, LI 22(3); Schane 1975, Essays on the Sound Pattern of English) are papers on English word stress that Glottolog attached to this language by a 'computerized assignment from "noncyclic"' (stated in both Glottolog records); relevance other-language, priority none.archive.org, Glottolog and the Centre Aequatoria site. The Aequatoria site turned out to host an open PDF of Motingea Mangulu 1990, Parlers riverains de l'entre Ubangi-Zaïre (Études Aequatoria 8), whose 'Esquisse du parler des Balói' (pp. 125-140, Likila dialect) was previously an access gap in our bibliography; downloaded (44 MB, scanned layer present) and read. Its phonology section (p. 126) says only that the tonology is of the normal Proto-Bantu type and that noun prefixes are generally low; nothing on stress or accent anywhere in the volume. Best available statement is therefore a tone-only statement, silent on word stress; no catalog's classification is contradicted or supported. Still unread: Bolongwa 1976 (Mbandaka mémoire) and Motingea 1996 (CNWS 43), neither located online.

new_statements.translation: c) The tonology is of the normal type (compared with Proto-Bantu). One nevertheless meets a few words with a tone pattern contrary to what one would expect in Lingombe or Lomongo: mbúlá 'rain', mai 'water'; bibende 'irons'... But since the tonology of certain Ngiri parlers shows peculiarities that generally depend on syntactic structure, it may be necessary here to await a more thorough study supported by tape recordings.
new_statements.citation: Motingea Mangulu, André (1990). Esquisse du parler des Balói. In: Parlers riverains de l'entre Ubangi-Zaïre: éléments de structure grammaticale (Études Aequatoria 8), pp. 125-140. Bamanya: Centre Aequatoria.
new_statements.locator: p. 126, §I. Phonologie, item c) (PDF p. 129 of the Aequatoria scan; render); also p. 126 §II 'Les préfixes sont généralement bas' and p. 129 §V 'Préfixes pronominaux: Leur tonalité est généralement haute, sauf pour les Cl. 1, 7 et 9.'
new_statements.check: confirmed by a second reader, with minor differences
new_statements.second_reader_evidence: Opened (open Aequatoria scan) and viewed the saved 200-dpi render plus fresh 110-dpi renders of PDF pp. 128-143 (print pp. 125-140, the whole Balói sketch), pp. 4-9 (Introduction générale) and pp. 277-279 (Conclusion, Notes). The quoted passage is at print p. 126, §I. Phonologie, item c), exactly as the reader gives it; the only differences are typographic: the page prints the open vowels 'lingɔmbɛ' and 'lomɔ́ngo' where the reader wrote 'lingombe'/'lomóngo', and the misspelling 'spécifités' is on the page as quoted. The scanned text layer ( line 5841) is badly garbled, so verification rests on the page image. Surrounding section: §I.a-b segmental notes (7 vowels, v, z, kp, NC clusters), §I.…
new_statements.rule_in_words: The language is described as a tone language whose lexical tone patterns are of the 'normal' (Proto-Bantu-conservative, non-shifted) type, with H and L marked on words (noun prefixes generally L, pronominal prefixes generally H). The source says nothing about stress or accent at all — no word-stress rule is stated, and stress is not mentioned as absent either.
new_statements.exceptions: A few words carry tones contrary to the Lingombe/Lomongo expectation (mbúlá 'rain', mai 'water', bibende 'irons'); author flags that Ngiri-area tonology is syntax-dependent and that a fuller study with recordings is needed.
new_statements.domain_note: Word-level lexical tone, citation forms from a single informant (Likila dialect); the syntactic-tone remark refers to phrase-level tonology in neighbouring Ngiri parlers. No stress domain stated.
new_statements.identity_note: The 1990 sketch describes the Likila dialect ('Notre description part du dialecte des Likila', p. 125; informant Bolongwa Bozenge from Ngondó village, recorded in Mbandaka) and explicitly treats Likila, Bangele, Bato ba lói and Lói as one language on the informants' testimony, i.e. balo1261 (Glottolog alt names Baloi/Loi/Likila/Rebu/Baato/Boloi). The 1996 CNWS chapter Glottolog attaches to biz is on Mpundza, a different Ngiri variety, and the two 'noncyclic stress' references Glottolog lists for biz are English-phonology papers mis-assigned by keyword.

new_statements.translation: c) The tonology is of the normal type (compared with Proto-Bantu). One nevertheless meets a few words with a tone pattern contrary to what one would expect in Lingombe or Lomongo: mbúlá 'rain', mai 'water', bibende 'irons'... But since the tonology of some Ngiri languages shows peculiarities that generally depend on syntactic structure, a deeper study, supported by tape recording, may have to be awaited here. [...] II. Nouns. The prefixes are generally low-toned.
new_statements.citation: Motingea Mangulu, André (1990). Esquisse du parler des Balói. In: Parlers riverains de l'entre Ubangi-Zaïre: éléments de structure grammaticale (Études Aequatoria 8), 125-140. Bamanya: Centre Aequatoria.

new_statements.reading: This is a tone statement, not a stress statement: the only first-hand phonological description of Loi-Likila that could be read describes the language as a lexical-tone language of the ordinary Bantu type and says nothing about word stress or accent placement. It is silent on stress; it does not license a stress-position coding. Bolongwa 1976 (Mbandaka mémoire) and Motingea 1996 (CNWS 43, Leiden; Grambank's source) remain unread and unlocated online (Leiden repository connection reset; abbol.com down
